prompt: You are an experienced data scientist and machine learning mentor. Please explain supervised learning to a beginner in a simple and easy-to-understand manner. Include the definition, difference between classification and regression, at least three real-world examples, the purpose of training and testing datasets, common machine learning algorithms, and explain when each algorithm is useful. Organize the answer using clear headings and a comparison table. Avoid unnecessary mathematical details.

Act as an AI research assistant. Explain how a neural network learns using backpropagation. Include a description of gradient descent, at least two examples of activation functions, and the role of the loss function. Do not include heavy calculus derivations. Present the answer in a step-by-step format.

You are a knowledgeable AI tutor helping a curious student. Explain the difference between supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning. Provide at least one real-world example for each type. Use bullet points for the examples. Avoid using jargon without explanation.

You are a senior software engineer mentoring a junior developer. Explain what a REST API is and how it differs from a GraphQL API. Include at least three key differences, mention common use cases, and provide a short code example for each. Do not skip the discussion of error handling. Present the comparison using a table.

Please act as a Python instructor. Explain object-oriented programming concepts including classes, inheritance, encapsulation, and polymorphism. Provide exactly one short code example for each concept. Avoid overly complex examples. Use numbered headings for each concept.

You are a coding mentor. Explain the difference between synchronous and asynchronous programming in JavaScript. Include at least two practical examples, mention common pitfalls, and explain when to use async/await versus promises. Do not include unrelated frameworks. Organize the answer with clear headings.

Explain how binary search works. Include the time complexity, a step-by-step walkthrough with an example array, and pseudocode. Avoid using an actual programming language for the pseudocode. Present the steps as a numbered list.

You are a data science consultant. Explain the process of exploratory data analysis (EDA). Include at least four key steps, mention common tools used, and explain why each step matters. Do not include unrelated deep learning content. Use a numbered list for the steps.

Act as a senior data analyst mentoring a new hire. Explain the difference between correlation and causation. Provide at least two real-world examples where correlation does not imply causation. Avoid overly technical statistical formulas. Use a comparison table to summarize the differences.

You are an experienced data engineer. Explain the ETL process (Extract, Transform, Load). Include a description of each stage, at least one real-world example, and common tools used at each stage. Do not skip data validation. Present the stages using clear headings.

You are a friendly high school teacher. Explain the water cycle to a student in simple terms. Include the main stages, at least three real-world examples of each stage occurring in nature, and why the water cycle matters for the environment. Avoid overly technical scientific vocabulary. Use a numbered list for the stages.

Act as a patient tutor helping a struggling student. Explain the Pythagorean theorem. Include the formula, a step-by-step example calculation, and at least two real-world applications. Do not skip showing the calculation steps. Present the solution as a numbered list.

You are an experienced history teacher. Explain the causes of World War I. Include at least four major causes, a brief explanation of each, and their historical significance. Avoid oversimplifying complex political relationships. Organize the answer using clear headings.

You are a business strategy consultant. Explain the SWOT analysis framework. Include a definition of each component (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats), at least one example for each, and how to use SWOT for decision-making. Do not skip practical application tips. Present the components in a table.

Act as a marketing expert advising a small business owner. Explain the difference between B2B and B2C marketing strategies. Include at least three key differences, common channels used for each, and provide an example campaign idea for each. Avoid generic advice without specifics. Use a comparison table.

You are a financial advisor explaining concepts to a new investor. Explain the difference between stocks and bonds. Include at least two risk factors for each, typical returns, and when each might be a suitable investment. Do not give personalized financial advice. Present the comparison in a table.

You are a network engineer explaining concepts to a junior colleague. Explain how DNS resolution works. Include at least four steps in the process, mention common record types, and explain what happens when DNS fails. Avoid unrelated networking topics. Present the steps as a numbered list.

Act as a cybersecurity expert training new employees. Explain what a phishing attack is. Include at least three common signs of a phishing email, one real-world example, and best practices to avoid falling victim. Do not include unrelated malware types. Use bullet points for the signs.

You are a cloud infrastructure architect. Explain the difference between IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS. Include a definition of each, at least one real-world example for each, and typical use cases. Avoid vendor-specific marketing language. Present the comparison using a table.

Explain how HTTPS encryption works to secure web traffic. Include the role of SSL/TLS certificates, at least three steps of the handshake process, and why encryption matters for user privacy. Do not skip explaining public and private keys. Present the handshake steps as a numbered list.
